about: Photo look with real space pictures: the biggest theories about the universe, clearly marked as theory.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, and STScI (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: Where the evidence runs out, theories begin. Some of today's wildest ideas may be tomorrow's facts. Most will not.

image.credit: ESA and the Planck Collaboration (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO)

scenes.narration: The Big Bang itself began as a doubted theory. Then, in nineteen sixty five, its afterglow was found.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, G. Illingworth, D. Magee, and P. Oesch (University of California, Santa Cruz), R. Bouwens (Leiden University), and the HUDF09 Team (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: Inflation says the universe grew enormously in a split second. Many physicists expect it to be right. It has not been confirmed.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, and STScI (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: If inflation never fully stops, our universe could be one bubble among countless others. A multiverse, untested so far.
Wormholes, shortcuts through space, are allowed by Einstein's equations. No one has ever seen one.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, D. Milisavljevic (Purdue University), T. Temim (Princeton University), I. De Looze (University of Gent) (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: The universe may end in a slow freeze, a rip, or a crunch. The freeze is the favourite. Nobody can be sure.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; J. DePasquale, A. Koekemoer, A. Pagan (STScI) (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: Each theory makes a prediction, and each prediction is a chance to be proved wrong. That is how wild ideas earn the right to be called true.
